content:
The image shows a corn ear with husks pulled back. Key observations:

- **Affected part**: Ear (cob)
- **Kernel color**: Mostly yellow/orange, appearing relatively normal
- **Husk color**: Distinctly pinkish-red inner husks — a hallmark sign
- **Pattern**: Pink/red discoloration concentrated on the husks and base area of the ear

The prominent **pink-to-red staining of the husks** is the defining visual characteristic of **Gibberella ear rot** (caused by *Fusarium graminearum*). This disease produces a characteristic pink/red mold that often starts at the tip and stains the inner husk tissues pink/red. Fusarium ear rot (also pink) tends to show scattered white-pink mold on individual kernels rather than husk staining. The husk discoloration here points clearly to Gibberella.
